decided to register for this gp following an incredibly negligent experience at Bradford medical, and this gp service is up and down. There are times where I have been listened too and received help, and others where its left me refused my meds, refused an appointment, or completely neglected.

Starting with the good because there is some here, once you bounce around the system long enough, the care beyond the gp is usually pretty good. The occupational therapist they have is an amazing person, and is one of the main reasons ive pushed through this practice. He's the main reason I have half the support I do, and im so incredibly grateful for all he's done. Even when i eventually leave he's promised to make sure I receive adaptations in my home to make sure I continue to be safe during treatment! Absolutely amazing gentleman, I cant fault him or what he's done for my care whatsoever!! 10s across the board for him!!!

Another good would be the two main GPS ive been seeing during my time here. The first, when she listens, is incredible. When she doesnt its a bit like shaving metal with a cheese grater but eventually things get done. 5/10, which I'll get too later on.

The 2nd is a bit better, he's mainly helped get me the physio I need, and listened to my concerns with as much care as a gp usually would, 7/10

Now to the bad, and oh boy itll explain the 1 star.
-refusing my meds. Its happened twice now because of the ask my gp service they use, that a gp, I believe Dr Hennessy, has refused to prescribe me my medication. He always seemed to do it whenever I stated id ran out of my prescription. Almost like he takes joy in seeing a patient on their last wits fight for mediocre pain relief, 0/10. If youre not involved in my care stop trying to screw me. You specifically have caused multiple pain flairs, multiple panic attacks, and severe distress. Get a hobby that isn't bullying youre patients.
-the receptionists seem to believe theyre qualified gps, which isn't appropriate whatsoever. They like deciding whether someone is ill enough for an appointment and if they deem you okay with a chronic illness then no appointment for you. 0/10
-the gps generally dont listen to youre concerns. I state one thing about my bodys reactions or day to day life, they say that its not accurate, even when i have photographic evidence. They will use any excuse too deflect from investigating or exploring treatment options, which has pushed me very dangerously close to a&e levels of pain or physical neglect. 0/10, pay attention to what youre patient is telling you babes.
- denying me an appointment due to moving. Im still registered with you, therefore im still youre patient. Just because you dont want me to be youre patient doesn't mean you get to stop treatment. 0/10.
-the health and wellbeing coach during my first session, told me my pain was all in my head, then after telling a nurse to take him off my care preceded to call me repeatedly to a point where I had to block his number. Either the nurse didn't do her job or he decide he desperately wanted to do his despite being told no. 0/10 it was embarrassing.

In future, id only dream of registering here for the OT. The rest of this practice is like a bandaid on a bullet wound. If youre fit and healthy, and get the occasional sniffle this practice will be good for you and will give you the care you need. If youre disabled, or chronically ill, this practice will be one to bounce you around before they so much as consider investigation. The only benefit I would say for you is the OT, and that's if youre condition impacts youre day to day activities.

You get 1/10 for the OT. Which makes you better than kill your patients Bradford medical (yay!) But care is still in the gutter and is in dire need of improvement before ill be happy recommending this practice for a patient of this practise for many years & I have to say that it really seems to be going from strength to strength. Have seen several ‘new’ people recently & all have been professional, thorough & friendly. Particular mentions for Muhammad Abdelkader & Darren Freeman who were both first rate. The Ask My GP Service is great for those of us who are able to use & have access to the internet & I would recommend logging your case when it opens at 8am, as I have always had a prompt response.
